subject: Vulnerability scan "Passport" + exception log for Brightline — evidence handoff
messages:
From: Laura Mills <laura.mills@brightline.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: security@brightline.com
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: ‘Passport’ scan bundle + exception details for SOC2 review

Hi Mina,

As part of our SOC 2 readiness we need the most recent vulnerability artefacts for the ‘Passport’ service (the model-serving cluster used by our sandbox). Specifically:

- the latest authenticated full-scan output (SAST/DAST/third-party scanner summary),
- a summarized CVE exception log for items older than 90 days,
- the current patching schedule for affected packages and expected closure dates.

Can you confirm the scan cadence for Passport (weekly, daily, or event-driven), and if Brightline can rely on Redwood’s SLA for CVE closure timelines for high/critical issues? If there are any SLA exceptions in the last 12 months, please include a short rationale.

We’ll accept a zipped bundle or links; our auditors prefer a single folder with a README. Target deadline is EOD Tuesday, 2028-06-20.

Thanks — appreciate a quick ACK.

—Laura
Laura Mills
InfoSec Manager, Brightline Financial
laura.mills@brightline.com

Attachments: none
From: mina_haddad@redwood.com
To: Laura Mills <laura.mills@brightline.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 11:05:14 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: ‘Passport’ scan bundle + exception details for SOC2 review

Hi Laura — thanks for the note and the deadline. ACK — we’ll get you a consolidated packet. Quick answers up front:

- Scan cadence: weekly authenticated host/container scans (every Mon), daily lightweight dependency checks, and on-deploy quick scans triggered by CI.
- CVE SLA: our standard target is 30 days for critical, 60 days for high, and 90 days for medium (exceptions documented).
- SLA exceptions: there was one operational exception for Passport in Q1 2028 tied to a vendor kernel patch; that’s included in the exception log with rationale.

I’m attaching a preliminary bundle: scan-passport.pdf (summary), cve-exception-log-2028Q2.xlsx, and a CSV with the upcoming patch windows. Ben (security ops) and Marissa (CISO) are looped for signoff and any privacy- or data-retention notes.

Action items:
- We’ll export the full authenticated scanner XMLs to the Drive link and send DocuSign for the evidence transfer.
- If your auditors need raw scan XMLs in a different format, tell us and we’ll repackage.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Security Programs Manager | Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

Attachments: scan-passport.pdf; cve-exception-log-2028Q2.xlsx; patching-schedule-202806.csv
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 08:22:31 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: ‘Passport’ scan bundle + exception details for SOC2 review

Mina — thanks for the quick turnaround. I reviewed the attachments and added a short findings sheet to the Drive (link below). A couple of clarifications before we ship final: 

- The Q1 kernel exception referenced was approved under ticket HS-5821; remediation schedule slipped due to vendor firmware dependencies. We have an auditor-facing note in the spreadsheet.
- Critical issue CVE-2028-1789 was mitigated by a compensating network control on 2028-05-03 and fully patched in the June 2 maintenance window; evidence (patch logs + rollforward) is in the CSV.

Decision needed from Marissa: do we sign the standard SLA attestation for Brightline (explicitly committing to the 30/60/90 targets) or propose the modified wording that calls out vendor-dependent exceptions? For SOC2 auditors we usually include both the standard SLA and an appendix listing exceptions.

Ben Carter
Security Ops Lead | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Thanks team — I reviewed Ben’s notes and the Drive artifacts. Mina, please publish the final evidence folder to the Drive link and include an auditor-facing README with the following elements:

- brief description of scan cadence and tooling (versions),
- CVE SLA table (30/60/90) with an appendix listing each exception + justification and ticket refs,
- patch verification artifacts (logs, build IDs) for any CVE marked as remediated,
- the chain of custody note for the exported scanner XMLs (who pulled them and when).

I will sign the standard SLA attestation but add an Appendix A that explains vendor-dependent exceptions; Laura, that should be acceptable for SOC2 reviewers provided the appendix contains the vendor timelines and mitigation notes.

Mina — once you upload the final folder, please send the DocuSign link to Laura and I’ll countersign. Also add a brief one-paragraph executive summary for Brightline’s auditor.
